sources.title: International AI Safety Report 2026

governance.definition: The policies, institutions, and accountability structures — set by governments and organisations — that determine how AI systems are built, deployed, and answered for.
answers: What happens when it causes harm?
levels: Government: statutes and regulatory frameworks (EU AI Act, India's Guidelines, US state laws)
Organisational: internal policy, risk management, oversight (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001)

safety.definition: The technical discipline of preventing accidents, misuse, and harmful consequences from AI systems — spanning alignment, robustness, monitoring, and evaluation.
scope: Frontier: loss-of-control and misuse risks from advanced systems
safety.relationship: Safety research produces the measurement and testing methods that governance rules depend on. You cannot regulate what you cannot evaluate.

sutras.name: Trust
sutras.gloss: AI systems should earn confidence through consistent, predictable behaviour.

sutras.name: People-first governance
sutras.gloss: Human wellbeing is the yardstick, not adoption speed for its own sake.

sutras.name: Innovation over restraint
sutras.gloss: Default to enabling development, with targeted safeguards rather than blanket limits.

sutras.name: Fairness and equity
sutras.gloss: Systems should not concentrate benefit or harm unevenly across groups.

sutras.name: Accountability
sutras.gloss: Someone identifiable owns the outcome of every deployed system.

sutras.name: Understandability by design
sutras.gloss: Systems should be explainable to the people they affect.

sutras.name: Safety, resilience, sustainability
sutras.gloss: Systems should hold up under stress, misuse, and long-term operation.

institutions.name: Data Protection Board of India
institutions.description: Statutory body established alongside the 2025 Rules; inquires into breaches and directs remedies.

obligations.summary: Itemised, plain-language notice. Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and revocable.
requirements: Itemised list of every personal data category collected
The specific purpose for each category
How to withdraw consent, as easily as it was given
How to lodge a complaint with the Data Protection Board
Retrospective notice for data processed before commencement

obligations.summary: Data may only be used for the notified purpose, and erased once that purpose is served.
requirements: Defined retention period per data class
Erasure on purpose completion or consent withdrawal
Data held by processors must also be erased
Security logs retained for one year

obligations.summary: Reasonable security safeguards, appropriate to the data and its risk. Carries the single highest penalty in the Act.
requirements: Encryption, obfuscation, or masking as appropriate
Access control and monitoring
Contractual safeguards flowing down to processors
Responsibility is retained even where a third party processes

obligations.summary: Affected individuals and the Board must be notified within 72 hours of a personal data breach.
requirements: Notice to affected data principals without delay
Notice must state what happened and what the person can do
Detailed report to the Board within the window
Detection and escalation tooling needed to make 72 hours realistic

obligations.trigger: Knowingly processing personal data of anyone under 18
obligations.summary: Verifiable parental consent before processing, plus an absolute prohibition on tracking and behavioural advertising to children.
requirements: Verifiable parental or guardian consent, with approved verification methods including DigiLocker
No tracking, monitoring, or behavioural profiling of children — prohibited even with consent
No behaviourally targeted advertising directed at children
Equivalent guardian consent for persons with disabilities who have a lawful guardian
exemptions: Subsidy, benefit, or service delivery, to the extent necessary

obligations.trigger: Designation based on volume and sensitivity of data, risk to data principals, and impact on sovereignty or public order
obligations.summary: Enhanced governance obligations for entities designated as significant.
requirements: Annual Data Protection Impact Assessment
Annual independent audit
Algorithmic fairness assessment for systems that could pose risk to data principals
Appointment of a Data Protection Officer based in India

obligations.area: Data principal rights and grievance redressal
obligations.summary: Individuals can access, correct, and erase their data, and must have a route to complain.
requirements: Access to a summary of data held and processing performed
Correction, completion, and erasure on request
Published grievance redressal mechanism and response timeline
Named point of contact for data queries

obligations.trigger: Personal data stored, processed, or shared outside India
obligations.summary: The Act permits the government to restrict transfers to notified territories. Operational detail is not yet notified.
requirements: Track notifications rather than pre-emptively restructure
Map current data flows so a future restriction can be actioned quickly

obligations.provision: MeitY India AI Governance Guidelines; IT Amendment Rules 2026
obligations.trigger: System uses AI or generates synthetic content
obligations.summary: Voluntary principles, plus binding rules on synthetically generated content and deepfake labelling.
requirements: Labelling and metadata for AI-generated content
Explainability proportionate to the decision's impact
Documented accountability for automated decisions
Human review pathway where decisions materially affect a person

penalties.breach: Failure to implement reasonable security safeguards
Failure to notify the Board or data principals of a breach
Failure to fulfil Significant Data Fiduciary obligations
Failure by a data principal to observe their duties

timeline.event: DPDP Rules 2025 notified; Data Protection Board established
MeitY publishes India AI Governance Guidelines
IT Amendment Rules on synthetically generated content notified

unsettled: Sensitive personal data categories await a separate Central Government notification.
Cross-border transfer restrictions remain deferred to future notification.
SDF designation criteria are set, but the list of designated entities is not yet published.
